title: Carry the box from the shelf to the bin (Unitree G1, walking, Pink IK)
text:
A steel shelving unit stands with its face 0.46 m ahead of the start pose, boards at 0.41, 0.76 and 1.49 m. On the middle board sits a brown cardboard box, 20 cm on a side and about 0.1 kg, its center 0.86 m up, nearly flush with the shelf's front edge and with 0.69 m of clear air above it. To the right, about 1.4 m away, a low table (top 0.53 m) carries an open blue sorting bin: interior about 48 x 72 cm around (1.81, -0.24), floor at 0.53 m, walls just 0.05 m tall — a shallow tray the box drops into, not a deep basket.
Goal: pick the box up off the shelf, carry it to the table, and leave it resting inside the bin. The task is complete once the box sits fully inside the bin's walls, released and come to rest — not still held, not straddling the rim.
The bin is further away than any arm reaches, so the box can only get there if the robot itself does — and the table stands off the shelf's axis, so the route turns.
success: Success, exactly (floor frame: origin at the robot's start spot, +y straight ahead toward the shelf, +x to its right, z up): (a) at some moment the brown box was taken off the shelf. Either its centre rose above 0.913 m (5 cm above its 0.863 m resting height), or it was held above 0.35 m inside the window in front of the shelf face (y between 0.063 and 0.413 m, |x| < 0.50 m). (b) At or after that moment, its centre came within 0.1986 m horizontally of the bin centre (1.8072, -0.245), i.e. it closed more than 90% of the 1.986 m start-to-bin distance. (c) At the end, the box centre has x between 1.6672 and 1.9472 m, y between -0.505 and 0.015 m, and height below 0.6666 m (0.136 m above the 0.5306 m table top, which excludes a box lying across the rim). Every component of its linear (m/s) and angular (rad/s) velocity is under 0.20. Not true at the start.
